best_for: Developers who live in the terminal and want AI agents, command blocks and shared workflows in it, and who are fine with a closed-source app that sends usage data.

points.title: Free works without logging in
points.text: Warp no longer requires an account; you can skip sign-up and use the terminal. AI and team features need you to log in, and after the first launch it runs offline without them.

points.title: AI usage is what you pay for
points.text: Free includes the agent CLI, pay-as-you-go AI add-ons and bring-your-own model keys for individuals and small orgs. Build lists at USD 18 to 20 per month with USD 20 of AI usage at API rates, Max at USD 180 to 200, and Business at USD 45 to 50 per user, depending on billing period. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: No Command Prompt on Windows
points.text: On Windows it supports PowerShell 7 and 5, WSL2 and Git Bash, but not `cmd.exe`. It needs Windows 10 version 1903 or later. On macOS it supports zsh, bash, fish and PowerShell and needs macOS 10.14 with Metal support.

points.title: Data collection to know about
points.text: Warp's privacy policy says it collects usage analytics and crash reports, and may store terminal content when you use cloud features or AI. It may use data to train its AI models; AI input collection can be controlled in settings.

points.title: Closed source
points.text: The app is proprietary. Warp has said it would open-source the client and server if the company ever shuts down.

points.title: Rolling back on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 145 versions, with user and machine installers for x64 and ARM64. macOS lists only the current universal build. Warp also offers Linux packages on its own site.
